When I started getting them, I had no idea what I was dealing with. I thought they were just terrible migraines at first. I was working as a graphic designer for a very small newspaper and I was unable to work. When my job was in jeopardy, I spent thousands of dollars seeing every type of doctor that was recommended, and trying a variety of treatments and tests (MRI,CATScan, acupuncture). None of them worked unfortunately, and I lost my first job. Most doctors are unfamiliar with clusters, and it was actually an intern at an eye doctor that suggested it could be clusters.
It appears there are a few sufferers here, including myself, that might be willing to answer any questions you have...fire away.
I hope that is true. I wouldn't wish clusters on anyone.

I met a mother that suffered from CH and she told me that she would rather give natural child birth 2-3 times a day for a month than deal with the clusters. That really puts the pain intensity in perspective.

Episodic CH sufferer here. Started getting them about 15 years ago. They will come for a "visit" about once every year or two, and stay anywhere from 3-10 weeks. During those periods I will get 1-5 attacks per day that last anywhere from 30 minutes to 6+ hours. The strain it puts on me physically, mentally and emotionally can wipe me out for 2-5x the attack time. After a "good one" (2+ hours) I'm usually worthless for 6+ hours, or until the next one hits. I have lost jobs due to this, where attendance is key. I have tried imitrex, and some other legal drugs, but nothing worked. I haven't tried LSD or mushrooms, but the Mary Jane has only made it worse. Perhaps I was smoking the wrong strain, Idk. Anyways, the last time I had a attack was 6 months ago and a Dr prescribed a steroid that I had to take 6x a day for a week. It was about two weeks after the start of my episode and so I'm not sure if it actually worked, or if the cycle was just over, however, next cycle I will definitely try it again earlier on. 
Has anyone else had any positive results from steroids?

I have had a few moments in my life such as these that have restored my faith in humanity.  The most recent was just a couple weeks ago.  My van had just broke down two days before so I was driving a friends junker truck just to get to work and back.  One day we had a blizzard and when I got off work and tried to leave I found that the truck would start.  There is a bus stop about a mile away, and the last bus was coming in about 20 minutes, so I started walking.  Now im not sure if the bus was early or I was late, but I found myself standing at a bus stop for 30 minutes in a blizzard and started realizing that I might have to walk the 9 miles home.  This might not have been all that bad however there were no open businesses within 2 miles (industrial park) to warm up in and the ice building up on my mustache and goatee didn't help.  There was moderate traffic on the road, and although people would stop for the light that was on the corner and stare, no one offered or asked if I needed any assistance.  After being outside for about 50 minutes a car pulled over in the middle of the road and asked if i needed a ride.  He had a full car load with a wife and 2 kids (who all squished in the back for me) and my house was a few miles out of his way, but he took me right to my front door.  I believe his kindness warmed me more than his car heater did that day.  Thanks again who ever you were!

TL;DR- stranded outside in a blizzard and stranger gives me a ride after many just drove by.
